brief: Nothing has changed on tonight's card, and that is on purpose. You have not logged a session since 3 August, so this morning's review saw exactly the same evidence the last one did, and three trainers looked at it separately and none of them found a reason to move a number. Every weight below is the same weight that was already sitting on your phone. That is the point: numbers should not drift while you are away from the gym, and this app has done that to you before. Tonight is Pull B, and it is now ten days since you trained and sixteen since you last touched this session. The row repeats 28 July exactly: 115, 135, 145, then 150. The top set asks for 9, the same 9 you already own, not the 10 you missed — a cold hinge after ten days off is not where you chase a rep you have never hit, and the 10 will still be there next time. Close-grip pulldown is the one thing higher than last time: 127.5 for 8 on all three sets. You took 120 for a clean 10, 10, 10, which is the top of that range on every set, so the step is earned outright, and 127.5 is not new ground — you pulled it for three sets on four separate nights in January and February. Eight reps instead of ten is where the time off gets paid back. Cable reverse curl sits at 35 for three sets of 12: at 37.5 your reps ran 12, 11, 10 against a slot that asks for at least 12, so the weight was wrong, not you. It is the last lift of the night, and the last lift is the one you have been quietly dropping — two sets instead of three on 31 July, two on 3 August. It is three short sets. Finish it. The rest hold: straight-arm pulldown 37.5 for 13 across, shrugs 70 for 14 across, incline curls 25s for 10, 10, 10 — that third set is the whole job, you got 9 last time. Rest three minutes on the row, about 75 seconds after that. Four cards are still waiting on your plan screen and none of them has been answered yet; three are the fixes to complaints you wrote in the log yourself. Tapping through them takes under a minute and stops the program asking you for things you have already refused. Last thing, and it outranks every number here: you have one bodyweight reading since 4 January — 206 lb on 21 July, now twenty-three days old — and one cardio session in the whole log. You are about twenty-eight weeks out. Standing on a scale this morning is worth more to March than anything on tonight's card.
